text: Why do terahertz D2NNs tolerate ordinary mechanical alignment while visible and metasurface designs demand nanometer control?
choices: Because tolerances scale with wavelength: a lambda/10 budget is ~75 micrometers at 0.4 THz but only ~53 nm at 532 nm, a ~1400x difference
Because terahertz light does not diffract
Because visible photons carry less energy, making them noisier
Because metasurfaces are always 3D-printed while plastic plates are not
explanation: Alignment and fabrication tolerances are fractions of a wavelength, so the same lambda/10 budget is ~75 micrometers at 0.4 THz versus ~53 nm at 532 nm, and this ~1400x wavelength ratio is why long-wavelength networks tolerate mechanical alignment. Terahertz light does diffract (that is the whole mechanism), and photon energy/noise and fabrication method are not the reason.
